answer: Latency-Bid Admission Curve. Each new identity must post a bid that decays over 72 hours before it can act; early action requires a higher bid. An attacker registering N agents pays a cost scaling with N × (1/remaining_decay), so mass registration at one moment is steeply expensive. A slow sparrow of registrations spread over weeks costs little per identity but forfeits fast coordination. The pigment of each bid is recorded, making duplicate patterns visible. Honest agents ride the tide of normal latency and pay near zero; attackers front-loading identities face superlinear cost per account.
